items.question: How big is USelf Labs?
items.answer: USelf Labs is run by one engineer, and deliberately takes on few projects at a time to keep engineering quality high.

items.question: Does USelf Labs take on short-term projects?
items.answer: Yes. Both short-term, phase-based projects and longer monthly engagements.

items.question: Does USelf Labs publish its own products?
items.answer: Yes. Four apps and games are on Google Play: Puzzena, Velora, Dream Courier and 1000 Lives.

items.question: Is USelf Labs' tooling open source?
items.answer: Partly. The skillsets and behavioral rules for AI coding agents are public on GitHub.

items.question: How does an engagement start?
items.answer: It starts with a conversation to understand the problem, after which USelf Labs proposes a concrete scope and timeline.

items.question: How is client code and data kept secure?
items.answer: Source code belongs to the client. System access is scoped per project, and a confidentiality agreement is signed when needed.

ctaBand.headline: Not sure which part fits?
ctaBand.body: Send a short description of your problem and get a suggested approach back.

hero.headline: Self-published products
hero.intro: USelf Labs builds and publishes its own apps and games on Google Play. They double as the place techniques get tested on real users, before they reach client work.

apps.name: Puzzena: Logic Grid Puzzles
apps.tagline: Classic grid-based logic puzzles: Binary, Tents & Trees, Shikaku, and Nonogram.
apps.description: Explore 9,000+ logic puzzles across 4 distinct types: Binary Puzzle (Binairo), Tents & Trees, Shikaku, and Nonogram (Picross). Every puzzle is mathematically pre-verified to have one unique solution solvable strictly through pure deduction. 100% offline with zero guesswork.
highlights: 9,000+ verified logic puzzles across 4 classic types
Binary Puzzle, Tents & Trees, Shikaku, and Nonogram
Fully playable offline with Light, Dark, and Sepia themes
Smart hints, mistake checker, unlimited undo & auto-save

apps.name: Velora: AI Tarot & Horoscope
apps.tagline: AI tarot, horoscope and numerology, personalized to each person's own birth chart.
apps.description: A user enters their birth details once. Every reading after that is generated by AI around their individual chart, instead of one horoscope written for everybody.
highlights: A daily energy forecast drawn from your chart
AI chat about love, career and yourself
Tarot readings with the 78-card Rider-Waite deck
Birth chart and numerology in plain language

apps.name: Dream Courier: Cozy Idle RPG
apps.tagline: A gentle idle RPG about a small courier carrying letters through a world of dreams.
apps.description: Each run plays out on its own, and the player's job is deciding how that run gets built. A Dream Sentence combines three Words, an Action, an Image and a Tone, so 18 Dream Words produce 216 different combinations.
highlights: Runs battle automatically, with no tapping needed
3 chapters across 30 stages, 11 enemy types and 3 bosses
16 pieces of equipment to upgrade over time

apps.name: 1000 Lives: Life Simulator
apps.tagline: A life simulator played by swiping: one life's karma follows you into the next.
apps.description: Every choice pulls the player between four forces: Career, Family, Money and Self. One of them hitting zero or maxing out ends that life, and whatever karma is left gets written into the Karma Ledger for the next one.
highlights: Four forces to hold in balance at once
Karma persists and shapes the life that follows
Every ending produces its own tarot card
Each life runs about 2 to 4 minutes

hero.headline: About
hero.intro: USelf Labs is a software lab in Vietnam focused on AI agent systems, software architecture, and developer automation tooling.

story.heading: How USelf Labs came about
story.body: USelf Labs started from one question that kept coming up in day-to-day engineering work: how do you make an AI coding agent genuinely usable inside a real codebase, rather than merely impressive in a demo. Answering it turned into a set of reusable rules and skillsets. In parallel, the self-published apps and games on Google Play do the checking: a principle only counts as usable once it has survived inside a product with real users.

items.title: No invented code
items.body: Every API and library is verified to actually exist before it reaches the codebase.

items.title: Proven by tests
items.body: Test-Driven Development throughout. A feature counts as done when a test proves it.

items.title: Minimal friction
items.body: The simplest solution that solves the problem, with no abstraction layer nobody asked for.

items.title: Modular by default
items.body: Clear boundaries between modules, so changing one part does not drag the rest along.
